tool.name: faToTwoBit
tool.description: convert FASTA to the compact binary 2bit format
tool.command: #set $in_ext = 'fa.gz' if str($input.ext) == 'fasta.gz' else 'fa' ln -sf '$input' 'input.${in_ext}' && faToTwoBit $long $no_mask 'input.${in_ext}' '$output' ## Read every base back. twoBitInfo resolves only the index and the record headers, ## so a truncation inside the last sequence's packed bases leaves it exiting 0. && twoBitToFa '$output' /dev/null

param.label: Use 64-bit offsets
param.help: Write a long (64-bit offset) 2bit file, required for genomes larger than 4 Gb.

tool.help:
**faToTwoBit** — pack one or more FASTA sequences into the compact, random-access binary **2bit** format.
2bit stores each base in two bits plus side tables for N-runs and soft-masking, giving a small file that genome browsers and track hubs can index by sequence and position. It is the canonical assembly container referenced from a hub's `genomes.txt` (`twoBitPath`).
-----
**Input**
- `Input FASTA` — nucleotide FASTA, plain or gzipped.
**Output**
- A `twobit` dataset (magic `0x1A412743`).
-----
**Key options**
- `-long` — emit 64-bit offsets (assemblies > 4 Gb). - `-noMask` — drop lowercase soft-masking.
Pair with `twoBitInfo` to derive the `chrom.sizes` needed by `bedToBigBed`.
-----
**References**
- UCSC 2bit format: https://genome.ucsc.edu/goldenPath/help/twoBit.html - `faToTwoBit` source: https://github.com/ucscGenomeBrowser/kent/blob/master/src/utils/faToTwoBit/faToTwoBit.c - Pre-built binaries and the full usage text: https://hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu/admin/exe/linux.x86_64/FOOTER.txt
This wrapper exposes the options that matter to a Galaxy job. faToTwoBit also accepts `-stripVersion`, `-ignoreDups`, `-namePrefix`, which are either process tuning or write paths a job cannot use; run `faToTwoBit` with no arguments to see the program's own list.
